chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the major sins, and he said: They are seven in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام): kufr in Allah, killing the soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury after the clarification, consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, fleeing from the battlefield, and reverting to desert-life after the Hijrah.

He said: So I said, Are these the greatest sins? He said: Yes. I said: Is consuming one dirham from the wealth of an orphan unjustly graver, or abandoning the salat (prayer)? He said: Abandoning the salat (prayer). I said: Then you did not count abandoning the salat (prayer) among the major sins? So he said: What was the first thing I said to you? He said: I said: Kufr. He said: Indeed, the one who abandons the salat (prayer) is a kāfir, meaning without an excuse.

key_terms.التَّعَرُّبُ بَعْدَ الْهِجْرَةِ: reverting to uncultured desert-life after migration to the Islamic community
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury, the forbidden gain from interest-based increase
key_terms.الزَّحْفِ: the battlefield or advancing battle line
key_terms.الْكُفْرُ: disbelief in Allah; the first and greatest sin mentioned
key_terms.عُقُوقُ الْوَالِدَيْنِ: disobedience and undutiful conduct toward one's parents
key_terms.مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: the property of the orphan, whose wrongful consumption is a grave sin

ai.seo_question: What are the major sins in al-Kāfī, and why is abandoning salat (prayer) considered so grave?
ai.summary: This hadith lists seven major sins recorded in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام), including kufr, killing unjustly, disobedience to parents, usury, and consuming an orphan's wealth. It further teaches that abandoning salat (prayer) without a valid excuse is even graver and is described here as kufr, underscoring the centrality of salat (prayer) in Islam.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> about the major sins, so he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘These are seven in the Book of Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> – the disbelief in Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and killing the soul (unjustly), and disloyalty to the parents, and consuming the usury after the clarification, and consuming the wealth of the orphans unjustly, and fleeing from the battle field, and the adoption of pre-Islamic practices after the emigration (Hijra)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So these are the greatest disobediences’. Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘So is the consuming of one Dirham of the wealth of an orphan unjustly is more grievous or the neglecting the Salāt?’ Heasws said: ‘Neglecting the Salāt’. I said, ‘But youasws did not number the neglecting of the Salāt in the major sins’. So heasws said: ‘Which thing was the first of what Iasws said to you?’ I said, ‘The disbelief’. Heasws said: ‘So the neglector of the Salāt is a disbeliever, meaning (neglecting) from without a (valid) reason’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurara who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the major sins. The Imam said, ‘They according to the book of Ali (a.s.) are seven: Disbelief in Allah, Murdering a soul. Disregard of good relations with parents. Consuming unlawful interest from trade with evidence, Consuming the properties of orphans unjustly. Running away from the enemy in battlefield during an offensive and Alienation from religion after accepting it.’

I (the narrator) then asked, ‘Are these the biggest sins?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, they are.’ I then asked, ‘Is consuming one dirham from the property of an orphan unjustly a bigger sin or disregarding the prayer?’ The Imam said, ‘Disregard of the prayer is a bigger sin.’ “I then said, ‘You did not mention disregard of prayer among the major sins.’ The Imam said, ‘What was the first item that I mentioned to you?’ I said, ‘It was disbelief in Allah.’ The Imam said, ‘One who disregards prayer is an unbeliever (that is, he is considered as such for ignoring prayer without reason?)”’
